title: Paisley: Nail & Henna Studio
shortDescription: Paint nails and draw henna designs that change color over about two days.
fullDescription:
Paisley: Nail & Henna Studio is a colorful, calm place for children to paint nails and draw henna patterns. It has two rooms to explore, and nothing to sign up for.

The Salon
• Paint nails with big polish bottles
• Pick from six nail shapes
• Add gems, stars, hearts and flowers to each nail
• Decorate one nail with patterns, close up
• Ink a henna stencil that fills itself in. "You can't get it wrong."

The Studio
• Draw henna with a cone that feels real, in fine, medium or bold nibs
• Stamp motifs: mandalas, paisleys, vines, borders and jaali
• Try mirror drawing
• Use two layers, and undo when you need to
"You can make anything."
The Studio is free while it's new.

Watch it change
A finished henna design changes over about two days, just like real henna. It goes from dark paste, to bright orange as it flakes off, to red, and then to a deep reddish-brown.

A grown-up can choose one reminder for when the design reaches its deepest color, or switch to a quick two-hour version.

Skin tones and outlines
Choose one of six skin tones, or a plain coloring-book outline. Change it right on the painting screens with the round hand button.

Pictures
Save pictures to "My hands". Sending a picture first asks a grown-up a question.

A note for grown-ups about henna
In Paisley, henna is only ever paste, orange, red or reddish-brown, never black. "Black henna" contains PPD, which is not safe on skin, especially for children.

Easy for little hands
• No ads
• No subscription
• No account
• No internet needed
• No tracking
• Every button has a picture, so children who can't read yet can play

Made for children and suitable for the whole family.
